articles.title: I fine-tuned EVA-02 in a week to build a neural video retrieval engine for what CLIP still won't do [P]
articles.summary: TL;DR: After a manic 7-day sprint, I open-sourced a local video retrieval engine built to search massive unstructured video portals by visual poses, clothing details, camera angles, and motion cadence—ignoring uploader metadata at search time and running in minimal VRAM. GitHub: https://github.com/qn06142/eva02-neural-video-retrieval Why Existing Models and Search Fail Scrubbed foundation weights: Stock CLIP, BLIP, and SigLIP still have massive blind spots for specific body postures, unconventional clothing styles, and unfiltered visual concepts. Fragile fixed classifiers: My earlier ensemble of JoyTag, P-HAR, and FashionCLIP choked on blurry, compressed footage and rigid taxonomies where "thighhighs" misses "over-the-knee socks" or "from behind" misses "rear view." Broken platform search: Uploaders stuff 50 generic SEO tags per video, and single-thumbnail indexing completely misses a pose or outfit that only appears for 20 seconds in a 25-minute clip. articles.title: aws-emulator
articles.summary: aws-emulator Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so. It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great if you could download a single binary and use that as part of a standard test suite in other languages and on other platforms.
